Viewed Viruses are everywhere, and have been for a long time, but do we know their origins? Well, truthfully, the origin of viruses is a mystery, because how can something that needs victims to make more of itself emerge in the first place? Still, there are many ideas. Viruses may have been essential steps in the emergence of life, or maybe they started out as escaped DNA from cells that became really good at making copies of themselves. Maybe they are the descendants of truly lazy parasites that let others do all the work for them? The current thinking is that viruses probably emerged multiple times from different origins, but we simply don’t know for sure yet. Whatever the truth is, viruses are the most successful beings on this planet. There are an estimated 10,000 billion, billion, billion viruses on earth. In fact, if we put them all next to each other they would stretch for 100 million light years – 500 Milky Way galaxies wide.

Viewed YouTube has demonetized and age-restricted my most recent video that's covering the events in Darfur. YouTube gave me no information or timestamps about what was wrong with the video, other than it vaguely involving "violence". I appealed the decision, and a "human" reviewer confirmed it was not suitable for advertisers. This decision by YouTube is final, and only then do they tell you what was wrong with the video but give you no possible opportunity to fix it.

So what was wrong? The thumbnail depicted "graphic violence". The thumbnail shows a satellite image of a watering hole in Darfur surrounded by cattle that was taken by Google Earth in 2024. This image was widely circulated around the internet as evidence of massacres in Darfur, but it was quickly debunked as nothing but a watering hole surrounded by a herd of cattle drinking out of it. This is the image I placed in the thumbnail, because it is explicitly not violent and shows nothing actually harmful. YouTube, in its infinite grace however, has decided that that was worth nuking the whole video over, and has now given me no opportunity to even swap the thumbnail out for something different. All of the work put into the video is now making zero income for futurue projects.

I expected this to happen with this subject honestly, but I felt it was still important to release due to the seriousness of the situation. If you'd like to help, the best way to do so would be by signing up to Nebula here https://go.nebula.tv/reallifelore, and watching my Mad Kings series there. 

Thank you for reading through my venting on this situation. YouTube is extremely frustrating and opaque to work with at times like this.

Viewed There are countless species that roamed the Earth in the past, and although we can't travel to the past to see them, we can still learn about them with the help of paleontology, which studies the history of life with the help of fossils. 
Fossils are any sort of remains preserved from past geological ages. Those can be bones or shells, remains or imprints, or a big variety of things preserved in amber. The totality of all fossils on earth is called the fossil record and it is the most important window on the past we’ll ever have. 
Still, we also need some luck. For a dead animal to fossilize a number of things must go just right: the right environment, timing and conditions. And then the fossil needs to survive for millions or hundreds of millions of years and then get back to the surface, where we have to discover it before natural processes dissolve it.

Viewed Think of your parents. As a child, you spend basically every day with them. However, your time spent together begins to decline as you become a teenager and fight to develop your own identity. But even as a teenager, you still probably see them regularly, which changes as you enter your twenties, when most people move out.

Even if you make an effort to be with your parents for two full weeks each year for the rest of their lives, which covers the main holidays, birthdays and a bit extra, you’ve already spent more than 90% of the time you will ever spend with them, even if they grow pretty old.

The time you have with the people you love is precious. So make sure to call and see them as often as you can.

Viewed When you battle an infection and there are too many enemies, your macrophages call for reinforcements. Hundreds of thousands of neutrophils pick up their signals and move to the battlefield. 
Neutrophils are intense warriors that only live to kill. In fact, they are so enthusiastic about killing that they even destroy themselves a few days after birth so they don’t have time to accidentally harm your own from the inside. As soon as neutrophils arrive, they begin vomiting deadly chemicals at bacteria or devour them. They are so careless in their attacks, that they cause real damage to your own cells as well. Still, collateral damage is not really their concern. Some neutrophils go so far as to push their self-destruct button and explode, casting wide and toxic nets made from their own DNA, filled with deadly chemicals which trap and kill bacteria. Sometimes they can continue fighting even after that, even though they are sort of dead already. This is how much fun they have killing.

Viewed there is this weird trend of companies that make products that are "not made to be bought used"

I bought a router that has this tunnel feature where you can bond 2-4 connections together & have them all work together, where they either duplicate one another or they each send a piece of the data + parity. You can run your own server or you can subscribe to use theirs so you don't have to fuck with things. I bought it used & wanted to sign up to use their service. it's a cool device!!!! if you are dealing with unstable connections, satellite, 5G etc this is a great way to combine them so you can run a server off of it with no disconnects or reliability issues. 

the original owner had removed it from their account but it still didn't work. i sent a support ticket in to demonstrate that it was removed from original owner's acct, showed the transaction proof, etc... still didn't work. 

they said i should buy these new because buying them used comes with these problems. they DON'T recommend people buy used because the used items could be attached to accounts of previous owners who aren't aware the device has been sold & a bunch of other issues. no solution, in spite of everything i provided. 

 I thought of the theft argument upfront, and called their bluff. i got around it by asking if they could tell the "real" original owner I have their product & am happy to send it back to them at my expense. if you have the information of the original owner - that's amazing, it means you can facilitate the return of their property. i won't even ask for proof that it was stolen - just give me the info so I can send them back the thing I spent $900 on. i'm ok losing $900 & accepting I got scammed if this was stolen, as long as the original owner gets their product back I am happy.

i know this wasn't stolen, and that this is an excuse to prop up the sales of new products. next ticket reply was them allowing me to use what i bought & paid for & subscribe to the services i was looking to use. 

more & more companies have these weird FAQ entries where they discourage the purchasing of used devices. weirder still are people on their community forums who will suggest that it's "wrong" or you're weird/off/a cheapskate for wanting to buy something used.

buying used is totally legitimate. it is a fucking WASTE to spend top dollar on something new when a used item exists that is not being utilized by someone else. the people who claim you're poor for buying used

1. i am not poor: i simply don't want to waste money & resources for no reason
2. i used to be poor... what's wrong with that ???

i have a company with six employees.. most of the stations on the desks i bought USED, my car i bought USED, my phone i bought USED because these items having scratches or dents on them is fine to me.

maybe a camera lens i'll only buy new, people are savages. scratch on a camera lens is a genuine difference & worth a few extra hundred since the product is defined by the scratches, unlike an audio recorder or a drill. and underwear: always new underwear...

but never let someone make you feel like it's abnormal to buy used. and when hey say you were trying to save money... YEP, that's the point, that's not something to feel BAD about. it means you put your financial security of yourself & your loved ones above your belongings being shiny. wear that as a badge of honor. it's a point of pride.

rant over

Viewed Hello, Mark here, of the YouTube channel: ‘Jay and Mark’.

You what now? 

That’s right. Much as I have always liked the channel name Jay Foreman (solid, dependable, if a little unspectacular), I’ve always felt it fell some way short in relating to *me*.

And so, like Iago to Jay’s Othello, I have ‘poisoned his ear’, and convinced him we are now somewhat indisputably a YouTube double act that warrants an appropriate name. 

But… DON’T PANIC! This is not the start of a coup. I recognise, even value, Jay’s contribution to Jay and Mark, and this isn’t part of a longer-term plan to slowly push Jay out of his / our brilliant channel altogether, and slowly assert full control until all future content features only me, and contains at least one slightly distancing and pompous Shakespearean simile per episode. 

It’s not that. 

Definitely. 

But, I understand you might have some questions. As this is fresh news - sent to you, the faithful subscribers, before anyone else - I can’t pretend the below is a real FAQ, because nobody has asked a single question yet; let alone given me a chance to tally them into ‘extremely rare’, ‘occasional’, or ‘frequent’,  and answer as appropriate. Instead, I’ve had a guess at some of the things you might be wondering, if, indeed, you care at all: 

1. Is this the end of Jay Foreman as an individual? 

No. Jay will be allowed to continue to exist as an individual. Should he wish to post something that has nothing to do with me on this channel, he can and will. 


2. Is this the end of @markcooper-jones7494 as a YouTube channel? 

No. This highly valued platform (4.75k subscribers, zero videos) is still dormant, awaiting its grand debut at an unspecified and, frankly, entirely unplanned day in the probably quite distant future. Watch this space. 


3. Why is it called ‘Jay and Mark’, not ‘Map Men’? 

Great question. It was something of a toss up, and there’s no doubt we’re still ALL about the maps. ‘Jay and Mark’ just made a bit more sense in case either Jay, or I, choose to put something that isn’t Map Men on the channel. Plus, there’s already lots on there that’s just Jay, and that should definitely stay there because, to be fair, some of it isn’t bad.  


4. Is this part of a bigger rebrand? Is anything about the style / content of the videos going to change? 

No, and no. 


5. When is the book out? 

23rd October and the link is here, but I don’t see how that’s relevant.  https://lnk.to/mapmen
